history.dynasty: Traditional founding by Roop Singh Chauhan of Khatu (contemporary with the first temple, ~11th century); ghats rebuilt in later renovations
history.summary: NOT A TEMPLE - SACRED WATER TANK/FEATURE, KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED: Shyam Kund is a stepped rectangular sacred water tank (sarovar) a short walk from the Khatu Shyam Temple, not a temple building. Tradition holds that this is the spot where the head (sheesh) of Barbarika was unearthed - revealed after a cow's udder spontaneously spouted milk there - and Roop Singh Chauhan built ghats (steps) around it when he founded the first temple in 1027 CE. It is also popularly said that Barbarika donated his head here at Krishna's demand. Devotees take a ritual bath (snan) in the Kund before visiting the main temple; darshan is considered incomplete without it. Beliefs attached: the water never fully dries even in the semi-arid Shekhawati region, bathing cures skin diseases and removes sins, and some believe it grants the blessing of children. Separate sections exist for men and women; shoes and socks must be removed on the premises. A small shrine to Goddess Shyam Maharaniji (believed to represent Barbarika's mother) stands beside it (verify). Coordinates are approximate - placed at the temple complex; the Kund lies a short walk away (verify exact location).

name: Shyam Kund
town: Khatu (Khatu Shyamji), Sikar district - sacred tank adjoining the Khatu Shyam Temple complex
town_description: Khatu (popularly Khatu Shyamji) is a pilgrimage town in Sikar district in Rajasthan's Shekhawati region, about 80 km from Jaipur. It is one of North India's most-visited devotional centres, drawing millions of pilgrims each year to the Khatu Shyam Ji temple and the adjoining Shyam Kund, with guest houses, dharamshalas and eateries serving the yatra crowd.

travel.railway: Ringas Junction is the nearest major station; a dedicated Khatu Shyamji station also serves the town (verify distances).
travel.road: A short walk from the Khatu Shyam Temple; well connected by road from Jaipur (~80 km) and Sikar (verify distances).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Phalguna Mela (February-March) is the peak pilgrimage - extremely crowded, plan accordingly.
